what: Fixes the pre-existing M100 limitation where consuming a columnar-aggregate output VALUE inside an enclosing expression (subquery/join/aggregate-ORDER-BY) failed with 'cache lookup failed for attribute N of relation 0'. Fix = Agg-swap rearchitecture (TimescaleDB pattern): admit stashes at upper_paths_hook (no CustomPath), standard_planner builds a normal Agg, and planner_hook swaps that Agg -> our CustomScan post-set_plan_refs with a plain-typed-Var tlist (no Aggref leaks). Swapped grouped result is ascending-sorted by group keys (Rust-side) to reproduce a GroupAgg's order; SORTED text-key GroupAgg left native.
hardware: DigitalOcean c-8 (8 vCPU CPU-Optimized dedicated), PostgreSQL 17.10 + pgrx 0.19.0
reproduce: benchmarks/columnar_composability_ab.py (1M-row theodb_columnar vs heap; four previously-failing shapes byte-identical + CustomScan; join; top-level regression check)
goal: columnar-aggregate output byte-identical AND consumable in subqueries/joins/aggregate-ORDER-BY, no top-level regression

composability_shapes.note: result correct via native inner plan

verdict: GOAL MET. Columnar-aggregate output consumable in subqueries/joins/aggregate-ORDER-BY, byte-identical to native, closing the pre-existing M100 composability limitation. No regression to M114 aggregate breadth, GROUP BY pushdown, or the top-level path. Fix = TimescaleDB Agg-swap pattern, reached after three empirically-disproven CustomPath-level attempts (honest, non-workaround).
caveats: AGG_SORTED (GroupAgg) over a text group key left native (collation-order safety); MIXED (grouping sets) out of scope; swap matches stashed admit to planned Agg by base-table OID (first unconsumed) — ambiguous multi-aggregate-same-table falls back to native.
